_about: Malady Wise fields bank: every medical, surgical, nursing, midwifery, dental, pharmacy, allied health, research/lab and health-equity field, with puzzle seeds for every game. Monthly build: rotate through fields so each gets a turn (pick fields with the oldest or null last_used), adapt seeds to the game formats, double-check facts, set seed 'used': true and the field's last_used to the puzzle date. Fields marked gentle: respectful tone, jokes never target patients or groups.

clues: A 64-year-old long-term smoker has a swollen face.
The swelling is worse in the morning and when he bends forward.
He is breathless and his voice is hoarse.
The veins in his neck are swollen and do not pulse.
Dilated veins run across his upper chest.
A CT shows a mass in the right upper chest compressing a large vein.
cases.teaching_point: Facial swelling, distended neck veins and chest wall veins suggest SVC obstruction, most often from lung cancer or lymphoma.

zebritis.q: Name an oncological emergency

trivia.q: The 2018 Nobel Prize went to Allison and Honjo for blocking which immune 'brakes'?

Febrile neutropenia is usually defined with a neutrophil count below what?
BRAF V600E inhibitors were first approved for which cancer?

grandrounds.q: Who proposed the 'seed and soil' hypothesis of metastasis in 1889?
Paclitaxel was first isolated from the bark of which tree?

fields.name: Nephrology
fields.source: Medical Board of Australia, List of specialties, fields of specialty practice and related specialist titles (document dated 22 September 2025); Field of specialty practice within Physician

clues: A 24-year-old man who smokes is coughing up blood.
He has felt unwell and tired for two weeks.
His urine is dark and has blood and protein in it.
His creatinine has doubled in a week.
His chest CT shows bleeding in both lungs.
His anti-glomerular basement membrane antibody is positive.
cases.teaching_point: Coughing up blood with rapidly failing kidneys is a pulmonary-renal syndrome; anti-GBM antibodies point to Goodpasture syndrome.

zebritis.q: Name a cause of a high potassium

trivia.q: Chronic kidney disease includes an eGFR below what for more than 3 months?
The first successful kidney transplant, in 1954, was between whom?
What is the leading cause of new kidney failure in Australia?
Australia's analgesic nephropathy epidemic in the mid-20th century was blamed mainly on which drug in compound powders?

grandrounds.q: Who built the first practical artificial kidney, a rotating drum dialyser, in 1943?
Fanconi syndrome affects which part of the nephron?

fields.name: Neurology
fields.source: Medical Board of Australia, List of specialties, fields of specialty practice and related specialist titles (document dated 22 September 2025); Field of specialty practice within Physician

clues: A 34-year-old woman's eyelids droop by the evening.
She sees double when she watches TV at night.
Her jaw tires halfway through a steak.
Her voice fades the longer she talks.
Everything is better after a rest.
Her acetylcholine receptor antibodies are positive.
cases.teaching_point: Weakness that worsens with use and recovers with rest, especially affecting the eyes, suggests myasthenia gravis.

zebritis.q: Name a cranial nerve

trivia.q: A positive Babinski sign means what happens to the big toe?
What did James Parkinson call the disease in his 1817 essay?
An electric shock down the spine when bending the neck (Lhermitte sign) is a classic clue to what?
Which cranial nerve has the longest course inside the skull?

grandrounds.q: Which nerve is injured in 'Saturday night palsy'?
Damage to which brain area, described in 1861, causes expressive aphasia?

fields.source: Medical Board of Australia, List of specialties, fields of specialty practice and related specialist titles (document dated 22 September 2025); Field of specialty practice within both Physician and Radiology

clues: A 40-year-old woman had a cold three weeks ago.
Now the front of her neck is very tender.
The pain spreads up to her jaw and ears.
She has palpitations and feels hot.
Her TSH is suppressed, her T4 is high and her ESR is raised.
A technetium thyroid scan shows almost no uptake.
cases.teaching_point: A painful tender thyroid after a virus with thyrotoxicosis and very low uptake on scan is subacute thyroiditis, not Graves disease.

zebritis.q: Name a radionuclide used in medicine

trivia.q: Most of Australia's molybdenum-99, used to make technetium-99m, is produced where?
trivia.a: ANSTO's OPAL reactor at Lucas Heights, Sydney

What is the half-life of technetium-99m?
FDG PET scans light up tissues that take up a lot of what?

grandrounds.q: Which American physician first used radioactive iodine to treat hyperthyroidism, in 1941?
Who won the 1943 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for using isotopes as tracers?

fields.name: Respiratory and sleep medicine
fields.source: Medical Board of Australia, List of specialties, fields of specialty practice and related specialist titles (document dated 22 September 2025); Field of specialty practice within Physician

clues: A 42-year-old man is increasingly breathless.
He smoked lightly for a few years in his twenties.
His spirometry shows fixed airflow obstruction.
His CT shows emphysema mostly at the lung bases.
His liver enzymes are mildly raised.
His brother was diagnosed with 'COPD' at 45.
cases.teaching_point: Emphysema at a young age, at the lung bases, or with a family history should prompt an alpha-1 antitrypsin level.

zebritis.q: Name a cause of finger clubbing

trivia.q: A smoker with COPD develops finger clubbing. What should this prompt a search for?
wrong: Nothing, it is expected in COPD

trivia.q: Using the GOLD fixed ratio, airflow obstruction is an FEV1/FVC below what?
The Epworth Sleepiness Scale was created in 1991 by which Melbourne physician?
Which Sydney physician invented CPAP for obstructive sleep apnoea in 1980?

grandrounds.q: 'Pickwickian syndrome' is now known by what name?
Rene Laennec invented the stethoscope in 1816 partly to avoid doing what?
grandrounds.a: Putting his ear directly on a young woman's chest

fields.name: Rheumatology
fields.source: Medical Board of Australia, List of specialties, fields of specialty practice and related specialist titles (document dated 22 September 2025); Field of specialty practice within Physician

clues: A 74-year-old woman has a new headache over her right temple.
Her scalp hurts when she brushes her hair.
Her jaw aches after chewing for a while.
Yesterday the vision in her right eye blurred for a few minutes.
Her ESR and CRP are very high.
Her right temporal artery is thickened, tender and has no pulse.
cases.teaching_point: A new headache over 50 with scalp tenderness, jaw claudication and raised inflammatory markers is giant cell arteritis until proven otherwise; vision is at risk.

zebritis.q: Name a form of vasculitis
zebritis.source: 2012 Revised International Chapel Hill Consensus Conference Nomenclature of Vasculitides

trivia.q: Under polarised light, gout crystals are needle-shaped and how birefringent?
The Schober test measures what?
trivia.a: How far the lower back can bend forward

trivia.q: HLA-B27 is most strongly linked to which condition?
Alongside swan neck, which finger deformity is classic in rheumatoid arthritis?

grandrounds.q: Gottron papules over the knuckles are a sign of which disease?
Which former antimalarial is a mainstay of lupus treatment and needs regular eye screening?

fields.name: Psychiatry
fields.source: Medical Board of Australia, List of specialties, fields of specialty practice and related specialist titles (document dated 22 September 2025)

clues: A 29-year-old man was started on haloperidol in hospital four days ago.
He now has a temperature of 39.5.
His muscles are rigid like lead pipes.
He is confused and hard to rouse.
His blood pressure and heart rate swing up and down.
His CK is massively raised.
cases.teaching_point: Fever, lead-pipe rigidity, confusion and autonomic instability after starting an antipsychotic is neuroleptic malignant syndrome, a medical emergency.

zebritis.q: Name a psychological defence mechanism

trivia.q: Australian psychiatrist John Cade discovered the effect of lithium in 1949 in which city?
Clozapine needs regular blood tests mainly to check for what?
trivia.a: A dangerous drop in white cells (neutropenia)

trivia.q: In which year was DSM-5-TR published?
In Capgras delusion, a person believes what?
trivia.a: Someone close has been replaced by an identical impostor

grandrounds.q: In Cotard delusion, what does the person believe?
grandrounds.a: That they are dead, or do not exist

grandrounds.q: Which two French psychiatrists introduced chlorpromazine into psychiatry in 1952?

fields.name: Public health medicine
fields.source: Medical Board of Australia, List of specialties, fields of specialty practice and related specialist titles (document dated 22 September 2025)

clues: A 68-year-old man who smokes has a high fever and cough.
He is confused and has diarrhoea.
His sodium is low.
His chest X-ray shows pneumonia in two lobes.
His urine tests positive for Legionella antigen.
Three other people who work on the same city street are in hospital with pneumonia.
cases.teaching_point: Pneumonia with confusion, diarrhoea and low sodium suggests Legionella; a cluster prompts a public health hunt for a source such as a cooling tower.

zebritis.q: Name a WHO-listed neglected tropical disease
zebritis.source: World Health Organization list of neglected tropical diseases (2024)
answers: Mycetoma, chromoblastomycosis and other deep mycoses

trivia.q: In 1854, John Snow removed the handle of a water pump on which London street?
Smallpox was declared eradicated in which year?

Australia became the first country to require plain tobacco packaging in which year?

Australia's 1987 'Grim Reaper' television campaign was about which disease?

fields.name: Radiation oncology
fields.source: Medical Board of Australia, List of specialties, fields of specialty practice and related specialist titles (document dated 22 September 2025)

clues: A 70-year-old man has prostate cancer that has spread to his bones.
For three weeks he has had worsening mid-back pain.
The pain is worse lying down and wakes him at night.
His legs now feel heavy and he has stumbled twice.
He has a band of numbness around his chest.
He has not passed urine since this morning.
cases.teaching_point: New back pain in someone with cancer, especially with leg weakness or bladder change, needs an urgent whole-spine MRI for cord compression.

zebritis.q: Name a radiotherapy technique

trivia.q: What is the unit of absorbed radiation dose?
Australia's first proton therapy centre, the Australian Bragg Centre, is in which city?
Why is radiotherapy usually split into many small daily doses (fractions)?
trivia.a: Healthy tissue can repair between doses

trivia.q: Wilhelm Rontgen discovered X-rays in which year?

grandrounds.q: What is the 'abscopal effect'?
grandrounds.a: Shrinkage of tumours outside the area that was irradiated

grandrounds.q: What is the Bragg peak?
grandrounds.a: The depth at which protons deposit most of their energy, then stop

fields.name: Diagnostic radiology
fields.source: Medical Board of Australia, List of specialties, fields of specialty practice and related specialist titles (document dated 22 September 2025); Field of specialty practice within Radiology

clues: A 58-year-old man with poorly controlled blood pressure has sudden severe chest pain.
He describes it as tearing, and it shoots through to his back.
The blood pressure in his right arm is much higher than in his left.
His ECG shows no heart attack.
His chest X-ray shows a widened mediastinum.
A CT aortogram shows a flap inside the aorta.
cases.teaching_point: Tearing chest pain to the back with unequal arm pressures suggests aortic dissection; CT angiography shows the intimal flap.

zebritis.q: Name a classic named sign in radiology

trivia.q: Wilhelm Rontgen's famous first X-ray picture showed whose hand?
On CT, water has a value of 0 Hounsfield units. What is air?
On a T2-weighted MRI, what usually looks bright?
Godfrey Hounsfield built the first CT scanner while working for which company?

grandrounds.q: Which South African-born physicist shared the 1979 Nobel Prize with Hounsfield for CT?
What is a 'Hampton hump'?
grandrounds.a: A wedge-shaped, pleural-based opacity from a pulmonary infarct

fields.name: Diagnostic ultrasound
fields.source: Medical Board of Australia, List of specialties, fields of specialty practice and related specialist titles (document dated 22 September 2025); Field of specialty practice within Radiology

clues: A 14-year-old boy wakes at 3 am with sudden severe pain in his left testicle.
He has vomited twice.
The left testicle sits higher than the right.
It lies horizontally rather than vertically.
Stroking his inner thigh does not lift the testicle (absent cremasteric reflex).
Doppler ultrasound shows no blood flow to the left testicle.
cases.teaching_point: Sudden testicular pain with a high-riding, horizontal testis is torsion until proven otherwise; surgery should not wait for imaging.

zebritis.q: Name an ultrasound artefact

trivia.q: Raising the frequency of an ultrasound probe does what?
trivia.a: Sharpens the image but reduces how deep it can see

trivia.q: Why is gel used in ultrasound scans?
trivia.a: To remove air between the probe and the skin

trivia.q: Who discovered the piezoelectric effect behind ultrasound probes, in 1880?
On lung ultrasound, multiple B-lines suggest what?
trivia.a: Fluid in the lung tissue, such as pulmonary oedema

grandrounds.q: In M-mode lung ultrasound, which sign suggests a pneumothorax?
Which Austrian physicist described the effect behind Doppler ultrasound in 1842?

clues: A 35-year-old man has a complete spinal cord injury at T4.
He suddenly develops a pounding headache.
His face is flushed and sweaty above the level of injury.
His blood pressure is 210/110.
His heart rate has dropped to 48.
His urinary catheter is kinked and his bladder is full.
cases.teaching_point: A sudden severe rise in blood pressure with headache in someone with a high spinal cord injury is autonomic dysreflexia; a blocked catheter is the classic trigger.

zebritis.q: Name a member of a rehabilitation team

trivia.q: In rehabilitation, what does FIM stand for?

trivia.a: A complete injury, with no sensation or movement in the lowest sacral segments

Who popularised mirror-box therapy for phantom limb pain?

grandrounds.q: Which neurologist founded the 1948 Stoke Mandeville Games, forerunner of the Paralympics?
Autonomic dysreflexia typically occurs with spinal cord injuries at or above which level?

fields.name: Sexual health medicine
fields.source: Medical Board of Australia, List of specialties, fields of specialty practice and related specialist titles (document dated 22 September 2025)

clues: A 27-year-old has felt flu-like for two weeks.
A rash of coppery spots has appeared on the body.
The rash is not itchy and includes the palms and soles.
There are patches of hair loss on the scalp.
Lymph nodes are enlarged in the neck and groin.
A painless sore healed by itself about two months ago.
cases.teaching_point: A non-itchy rash involving the palms and soles, with a past painless sore, should prompt syphilis testing; rates have risen sharply in Australia.

zebritis.q: Name a sexually transmissible infection

trivia.q: HIV PrEP was listed on Australia's PBS in which year?
In HIV care, what does U=U mean?

cases.diagnosis: Relative energy deficiency in sport (RED-S) with tibial stress fracture
clues: A 19-year-old distance runner has pain in her right shin.
It began only during runs but now aches at rest.
She has upped her training for a marathon.
Her periods stopped eight months ago.
She has lost weight and her BMI is low.
A bone density scan shows low bone mass for her age.
cases.teaching_point: Missed periods, low energy availability and stress fractures in an athlete suggest RED-S; it affects bone, hormones and performance.

zebritis.q: Name an injury or condition named after a sport or activity

trivia.q: Which test is the most sensitive bedside check for an ACL tear?
Osgood-Schlatter disease affects which spot?
trivia.a: The bony bump below the kneecap (tibial tuberosity)

trivia.q: What does VO2 max measure?
trivia.a: The maximum rate the body can use oxygen

trivia.q: What is commotio cordis?
trivia.a: Cardiac arrest from a blow to the chest at a vulnerable moment in the heartbeat

grandrounds.q: Which Canadian emergency physician led the 1992 study that produced the Ottawa ankle rules?
Which tendon is torn or avulsed in a mallet finger?
grandrounds.a: The terminal extensor tendon at the DIP joint

fields.name: Cardio-thoracic surgery
fields.source: Medical Board of Australia, List of specialties, fields of specialty practice and related specialist titles (document dated 22 September 2025); Field of specialty practice within Surgery

clues: A 68-year-old man is on day 2 after coronary bypass surgery.
His blood pressure is falling despite fluids.
His neck veins are distended and his central venous pressure is rising.
His heart sounds are hard to hear.
His chest drains, which were draining steadily, have suddenly stopped.
His blood pressure drops more than 10 mmHg when he breathes in.
cases.teaching_point: Falling blood pressure, rising venous pressure and muffled heart sounds after heart surgery (Beck's triad) suggest tamponade; drains that suddenly stop can be a clue.

zebritis.q: Name a cardiac or thoracic operation

trivia.q: Who performed the first human heart transplant, in Cape Town in 1967?
Pioneering heart transplant surgeon Victor Chang worked at which Sydney hospital?
Who first used a heart-lung machine successfully in a human, in 1953?

What does TAVI stand for?

fields.name: General surgery
fields.source: Medical Board of Australia, List of specialties, fields of specialty practice and related specialist titles (document dated 22 September 2025); Field of specialty practice within Surgery

clues: A 78-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation has sudden severe tummy pain.
She stopped her blood thinner a fortnight ago.
She is writhing in pain.
Yet her abdomen is soft and only mildly tender.
She has vomited and passed a loose stool.
Her lactate is high.
cases.teaching_point: Severe abdominal pain out of proportion to the examination in someone with AF suggests mesenteric ischaemia; CT angiography is urgent.

zebritis.q: Name a type of abdominal wall or abdominal hernia

fields.name: Neurosurgery
fields.source: Medical Board of Australia, List of specialties, fields of specialty practice and related specialist titles (document dated 22 September 2025); Field of specialty practice within Surgery

clues: A 19-year-old is hit on the side of the head by a cricket ball.
He is knocked out for a few seconds.
He then gets up, feels fine and keeps playing.
Three hours later he has a worsening headache and vomits.
He becomes drowsy and his left pupil is large.
CT shows a lens-shaped bleed over the left temple.
cases.teaching_point: A lucid interval after a blow to the temple, then deterioration, suggests an extradural haematoma, usually from the middle meningeal artery.

zebritis.q: Name a type of primary brain tumour
zebritis.source: WHO Classification of Tumours of the Central Nervous System (2021)

trivia.q: Who is widely called the father of modern neurosurgery?
Cushing's triad of raised intracranial pressure is high blood pressure, irregular breathing and what?

grandrounds.q: Name a clinical grading scale for subarachnoid haemorrhage.
grandrounds.a: Hunt and Hess, or the WFNS scale

grandrounds.q: Which artery is usually torn in an extradural haematoma?

fields.name: Orthopaedic surgery
fields.source: Medical Board of Australia, List of specialties, fields of specialty practice and related specialist titles (document dated 22 September 2025); Field of specialty practice within Surgery

clues: A 12-year-old boy has had a sore left knee for six weeks.
He has started limping.
He is tall for his age and heavier than average.
His left foot turns outwards when he walks.
Turning his left hip inwards is painful and restricted.
A frog-leg hip X-ray shows the femoral head slipping off the neck.
cases.teaching_point: Knee pain in an overweight early teen with reduced hip internal rotation is SCFE until proven otherwise; hip pain often refers to the knee.

zebritis.q: Name an eponymous fracture

trivia.q: Scaphoid fractures are notorious for which complication?
The Garden classification is used for which fractures?
The Salter-Harris classification describes fractures involving what?
The Thomas splint, which slashed deaths from thigh fractures in World War I, was invented by whom?

What is O'Donoghue's 'unhappy triad' of the knee?

fields.name: Otolaryngology - head and neck surgery
fields.source: Medical Board of Australia, List of specialties, fields of specialty practice and related specialist titles (document dated 22 September 2025); Field of specialty practice within Surgery

clues: A 22-year-old has had a sore throat for five days.
It is now much worse on the left side.
He can barely open his mouth (trismus).
His voice sounds muffled, like he has a hot potato in his mouth.
He is drooling because swallowing hurts so much.
His uvula is pushed over to the right.
cases.teaching_point: A one-sided worsening sore throat with trismus, a muffled voice and a deviated uvula suggests a peritonsillar abscess (quinsy).

zebritis.q: Name a structure of the middle or inner ear

trivia.q: What is the smallest bone in the human body?
Which Australian led the development of the multichannel cochlear implant, first implanted in 1978?
Most nosebleeds come from which area?
trivia.a: Little's area at the front of the nasal septum

grandrounds.q: What triad makes up Gradenigo syndrome?

grandrounds.q: Frey syndrome, sweating while eating, typically follows surgery on which gland?

fields.name: Oral and maxillofacial surgery
fields.source: Medical Board of Australia, List of specialties, fields of specialty practice and related specialist titles (document dated 22 September 2025); Field of specialty practice within Surgery

clues: A 35-year-old man has had a painful lower back tooth for a week.
Now the floor of his mouth is swollen on both sides.
His tongue is pushed up and back.
He is drooling and cannot swallow.
The front of his neck feels woody and hard.
He has a fever and his voice is muffled.
cases.teaching_point: Bilateral floor-of-mouth swelling with a raised tongue after a dental infection is Ludwig's angina; the airway is the immediate danger.

zebritis.q: Name a bone of the skull

trivia.q: Le Fort fractures classify fractures of which part of the face?
A Le Fort III fracture separates what?
In Australia, oral and maxillofacial surgeons hold which degrees?
Osteonecrosis of the jaw is a rare side effect linked to which medicines?

grandrounds.q: Which sequence combines a small jaw, a tongue that falls back and a cleft palate?

The vomiting is forceful and shoots across the room.
The vomit is milky, not green.
He seems hungry again straight after vomiting.
He is losing weight and has fewer wet nappies.
An olive-sized lump can be felt in the upper abdomen during a test feed.
cases.teaching_point: Projectile non-bilious vomiting in a hungry baby of 2 to 8 weeks is pyloric stenosis; it causes a low-chloride, low-potassium metabolic alkalosis.

zebritis.q: Name a congenital condition treated by paediatric surgeons

trivia.q: Exomphalos and gastroschisis both leave bowel outside the tummy. Which one has a covering sac?
In the VACTERL association, what does 'TE' stand for?
In hypospadias, where is the urethral opening?

What is the name of the most common, posterolateral type of congenital diaphragmatic hernia?

cases.diagnosis: Flexor tenosynovitis after a cat bite

The whole finger is now swollen like a sausage.
She holds it slightly bent.
Trying to straighten it is extremely painful.
It is tender all along the front of the finger.
She has a fever and red streaks up her forearm.
cases.teaching_point: Kanavel's signs after a bite (fusiform swelling, flexed posture, pain on passive extension, tenderness along the sheath) mean flexor sheath infection needing urgent surgical care.

Harold Gillies pioneered facial reconstruction for soldiers injured in which war?

cryptic.definition: Skin moved with its blood supply, or a panic

fields.name: Urology
fields.source: Medical Board of Australia, List of specialties, fields of specialty practice and related specialist titles (document dated 22 September 2025); Field of specialty practice within Surgery

clues: A 60-year-old man who smokes notices blood in his urine.
It is painless and comes and goes.
He has a dull ache in his left side.

cases.teaching_point: Painless haematuria needs investigation; a new left varicocele that does not empty lying down can point to a left kidney tumour.

zebritis.q: Name a cause of blood in the urine in an adult

trivia.q: A vasectomy cuts which tube?

What is the biggest modifiable risk factor for bladder cancer?

clues: A 74-year-old man who has smoked all his life has sudden severe back pain.
The pain also spreads to his tummy and groin.
He collapses at home.
His blood pressure is 80/50 and he is pale and sweaty.
There is a pulsating mass in his upper abdomen.
A bedside ultrasound shows an aorta 7 cm wide.

Buttock claudication, erectile dysfunction and absent femoral pulses make up which syndrome?
An abdominal aortic aneurysm is defined as an aortic diameter of at least what?

The night nurse notes she is quieter than usual and dozing through meals.
She answers questions slowly and loses track mid-sentence.
She cannot say the months of the year backwards.
